title: Resilient edge traffic degradation protocol for active-active API gateways
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a resilient traffic degradation protocol for Redwood's hosted API edge to support active-active multi-region operation while preserving streaming session continuity and SLOs. The work covers traffic-shifting heuristics, session-aware circuit breaking, tiered load-shedding, and runbook + automation for controlled degradation and rollback. This ticket scopes the implementation and validation (canary + chaos testing) for the initial rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy that can shift traffic by weighted percentages between regions with sub-100ms decision latency
Session-aware streaming handoff that preserves in-flight KV checkpoints for >=95% of active sessions during a 30s regional drain
Circuit breaker library with dynamic thresholds (CPU/GPU queue depth, token-latency percentiles) and per-tenant priority tiers
Load-shedding rules implemented that reduce p99 latency while sacrificing <5% of requests for P0 customers and configurable for lower tiers
Automated dashboard showing error budget burn, cross-region bandwidth, and session continuity metrics; alerts for emergency rollback
Runbook with step-by-step traffic-shift and rollback commands; tested in chaos drill with documented results
comments: 2026-02-12 Asha Patel: Initial scoping — pulled metrics from last 6 months to understand p99 tail during regional maintenance. Observed 2.4x p99 increase for streaming sessions when cross-region checkpoints are enabled naively.

2026-02-18 Marco Liu: Design review — recommend tokenized session handles + intermittent KV sync (delta checkpoints) instead of full KV copy during active handoff to reduce tail impact. Added prototype API for checkpoint pull/publish in edge-proxy.

2026-02-25 Design review notes (Sofia Gonzalez): For multi-tenant fairness, implement per-tenant graceful degradation priorities; don't allow lower-tier shedding to affect quotas for enterprise customers. Also: ensure RBAC gating for emergency traffic shifts.

2026-03-02 Engineering update: Implemented circuit-breaker abstraction; thresholds are CPU queue depth and 95th request latency per shard. Added a feedback loop that allows circuit to open for 30s with exponential backoff. See PR 820.

2026-03-05 Load-shedding heuristic experiment: Two heuristics compared — (A) earliest-deadline-first by request age and qos, (B) token-cost-based drop. A performed better for latency but increased cost. Decided to adopt hybrid: EDF for real-time streaming, token-cost for bulk generation.

2026-03-09 Canary plan: 5% of traffic to new routing for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn, session loss. Canary config in gateway repo under canaries/edge-degrade.yaml. Need runbook signoffs from support and infra.

2026-03-12 Chaos test summary: Ran simulated region outage for 90s against canary; session continuity preserved for 92% of streams (target 95%). Next action: improve checkpoint frequency and add incremental state sync to reach target. Observed increased inter-region egress by ~18% during resync windows — cost vs latency trade-off noted.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive checkpointing improves continuity but increases egress and can worsen p99 for non-affected requests. Preferred approach is adaptive checkpoint frequency triggered by signal (stream age, likelihood of migration) and conservative default. Operationally, provide support with a pre-flight checklist and automated rollback script to revert routing weights and close opened circuits.
observability_notes: New metrics added: edge.degrade.weight, session.handoff.success_rate, cb.open_duration_by_shard, shed.rate_by_tier. Alerts: SLO_burn_high (>30% in 1h), session_handoff_drop_rate (>5% over 15m).
next_steps: 1) Finish incremental checkpoint implementation (Marco) 2) Re-run chaos after checkpoint optimizations 3) Socialize runbook with SRE and Support 4) Schedule canary rollout in weekly deploy window
communication_plan: Customer-facing comms drafted: short notice to enterprise customers with mitigation knobs. Internal Slack incident channel pre-wired. Support KB entry for manual rollback steps.
